To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the production of a spin-2 particle is dominated by the exchange of a gluon pair in the s channel and is therefore suppressed by the small gluon luminosity at LHC energies, and that (ii) this suppression can be compensated by the production of a pair of spin-2 particle, which is enhanced by the large gluon luminosity, leading to a significant production cross section for a pair of spin-two particles.

we have developed a general and flexible implementation of graviton → jets processes in the MadGraph/MadEvent framework and validated it by comparing with the corresponding next-to leading order results.

the production of graviton ± jets can be described at the parton level by a simple effective theory with the energy momentum tensor as the only source for the graviton interactions with the standard model fields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the simulation of the production of spin-2 states at the LHC, with particular emphasis on the graviton case, and the study of the corresponding phenomenological consequences.
a detailed study of the production and decay properties of graviton states at hadron collid- ers.
a general study of spin-2 production at the hadron collider.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current experimental bounds on the ADD graviton mass and on the RS graviton mass are still far below the sensitivity that can be reached at the TeV colliders.
the current LHC data is not yet sensitive to graviton production, and that a discovery is possible only in the case that the graviton mass is very close to the kinematic threshold.
the graviton + jets production is an important background for many new physics searches at the LHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have implemented a very general and powerful framework for the simulation of the production of spin-2 resonances at the hadron collider, which is ready to be used by experimentalists for a wide range of scenarios.

we can generate samples of graviton + jets at the TeV colliders in several models, and we can validate them against the corresponding next to leading order QCD calculations.

The main takeaway from our work is that
graviton production is a very challenging task at hadron collider.
graviton production at the LHC can be simulated at the same level of precision and flexibility as other standard model particles.
gravitons can be produced at hadron colliding machines, and that their discovery can be pursued by means of a wide variety of channels, which are complementary and should be explored in parallel.
